title: Nurx vs FutureClinic: acne and birth control without the monthly fee
summary: Nurx vs FutureClinic compares acne and birth control costs without insurance, monthly fees, and a $40 FutureClinic visit with a physician by message.
body_markdown:
## What do acne and birth control cost over a year?


Nurx suits people who want the platform to bill private insurance for medications it fills, or who want a bundled package like its[Solstice menopause kit](https://www.nurx.com/menopause-treatment/) from $95 a month (as of October 2026). Nurx accepts most private insurance for medicines, though its[birth control cost FAQ](https://www.nurx.com/faq/how-much-does-birth-control-cost/) notes "we do not submit claims to insurance for the medical consult fee" and government plans are excluded. Per[Nurx's cost FAQ](https://www.nurx.com/faq/how-much-does-nurx-cost/) , birth control has a "$28 consultation fee" with a year of messaging and cash pills from $15 a month.


When paying cash for acne, ongoing fees add up. As of October 2026, Nurx charges a $40 acne consult fee plus a "flat $3 support fee each month" ($36 a year) "whether the order is filled through Nurx or at your local pharmacy". Cash topicals start at $25 a month (tretinoin cream is $60 for two months, or $360 a year) and oral generics run $15 to $30 a month (spironolactone is $45 for three months; minocycline is $40 for one month).


On FutureClinic, a visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100, with no subscription needed. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, so their only incentive is to help you and they never upsell you a medicine or lab panel. If your doctor decides it's right for you, they can prescribe whichever brand or generic fits (controlled medicines excepted) with no house formulary, including several months of a stable medicine at once when they judge it safe. Prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, with a cash discount coupon or insurance (FutureClinic helps with prior authorizations). Doctors also order discounted labs, and most offer an optional membership for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time, typically $25 to $100 a month.


## Where can you message a doctor for acne or birth control?


Nurx states on its acne page that "Services not offered in every state". FutureClinic works in 33 states and Washington, D.C.: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. Your doctor must be licensed in the state you're in, and if you do not see your state listed, try anyway as coverage grows.


Start at[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) or from your AI app at[https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) , where your AI can prefill intake questions from what you already shared, or send:


> ` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


FutureClinic is not for emergencies; call 911 in an emergency, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
